[ASSISTANT_SAID] Foods and drinks to avoid before bed for better sleep hygiene include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Caffeine: Coffee, tea, soda, and energy drinks.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Alcohol: Disrupts sleep patterns despite initial drowsiness.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Spicy, fatty, or heavy meals: Can cause indigestion or heartburn.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Sugary foods: May lead to blood sugar spikes disrupting sleep.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. High-protein foods: Require energy to digest, keeping you alert.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Nicotine: Interferes with sleep quality.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 7. Drinks with aspartame or artificial sweeteners: Can disrupt sleep.  
[USER] User was unaware that some regular foods and drinks hinder sleep.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Foods and drinks that can promote better sleep hygiene include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Warm milk: Contains tryptophan to help induce sleep.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Herbal tea: Chamomile, valerian, passionflower promote relaxation.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Cherries: Contain melatonin, which regulates sleep-wake cycle.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Bananas: Contain magnesium and potassium for muscle relaxation.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Whole grain crackers or bread: Increase tryptophan levels in the brain.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Leafy greens: Rich in magnesium, promoting relaxation.  
[USER] User plans to try including some of these foods and drinks in their bedtime routine.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Additional tips for improving sleep hygiene include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Set a sleep schedule: Go to bed and wake up at the same time daily.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Create a relaxing bedtime routine: Activities like reading or meditation.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Make bedroom conducive for sleep: Keep it cool, quiet, and dark.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Limit screen time before bed: Avoid electronic devices an hour before sleep.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Get regular exercise: Aim for at least 30 minutes most days
